image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house with a heavy chestnut front door, a large iron bear knocker bolted to it, and a rusted padlock hanging from a chain on the door frame

storyboard.claim: Peton is the cage and the iron bear is the padlock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The chestnut door of the timber house, close, with the iron bear knocker and a padlock on its chain so the bear reads as a lock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the new section on the house as a trap, after the chestnut door was just called a boundary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Re-casts the iron bear from a guard dog into a padlock on a cell.

left.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house with a heavy chestnut door and an iron bear knocker, lit by one candle at dusk

right.label: TODAY
right.subject: a present-day house with the same heavy chestnut door and iron bear knocker, lit by a porch lamp at night

storyboard.claim: The same iron hardware does the same job in 1692 and today.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two matched frames of the same door and bear knocker, one candlelit in 1692 and one under a porch lamp today.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the padlock image and carries the idea across the centuries.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that the lock is the house itself, not one era of it.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house at dusk seen through a tall iron fence, every window dark, no figure anywhere

storyboard.claim: The house is a machine that traps the people inside it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The timber house behind an iron fence at dusk with every window dark, so the house looks closed in on itself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the padlock metaphor into the whole building.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the fence, so the house reads as a barrier that holds people in.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, steps off the back porch of a timber house onto the grass at dusk and looks toward the far trees

storyboard.claim: Julia leaves the house and turns to the land around it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia in plain modern clothes stepping from the house's back porch onto the grass, looking out at the trees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the viewer from inside the house to outside it, as the narration says she leaves the safety of the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the first time Julia is outside, on the grounds.

image.subject: an overgrown back lawn behind a timber house, tall weeds and dark woods along the property line, a grey dusk sky, no figure

storyboard.claim: The backyard is the setting of the chilling scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wide untended back lawn with dark woods at its edge and no one on it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches from Julia to the place she is about to walk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the wild, empty ground before anyone is on it.

image.subject: Julia, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, walks through a wide untended field behind the timber house, far from any garden, at dusk

storyboard.claim: Julia is walking the huge grounds, and it is nothing like a neat lawn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia small in the middle of a wide, untended field behind the house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Julia into the empty backyard the previous frame set up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the scale of the land by her size against it.

image.subject: Julia, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, wades through weeds that reach her knees while wind bends the grass around her, the frame cut from her waist down

storyboard.claim: The weeds are knee-high and the wind is moving through them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia's legs pushing through knee-high grass while the wind bends it sideways.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms closer on Julia now that she is in the field.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the overgrowth physical, a thing that pushes against her.

image.subject: Julia, plain modern clothes, kneels alone at the edge of dark woods, looking down at a patch of freshly turned black dirt

storyboard.claim: She is completely alone at the woods edge and looks down at the dirt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia kneeling by a patch of dug black soil with the woods dark behind her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows from the wide field to the spot where she finds something.
storyboard.addedInformation: The turned soil is the first sign that something is buried there.

image.subject: a pale, weathered human pelvic bone lying half-buried in black soil, filling the frame, no body visible

storyboard.claim: She finds a large human pelvic bone in the dirt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A close, clean view of a pale pelvic bone set in dark soil, no body.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pays off the turned dirt with the thing under it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the shape clearly enough that a viewer can see it is a pelvis, not a small animal.

left.label: DEER
left.subject: a slim deer leg bone lying on dark soil

right.label: HUMAN
right.subject: a broad human pelvic bone lying on dark soil, the same frame and light

storyboard.claim: The bone is a human pelvis, not a deer femur.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two matched frames of bone on dark soil: a thin deer leg bone beside a wide human pelvis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms what the previous frame showed and rules out the easy explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Teaches the difference by shape, so a muted viewer can tell the two apart.

image.subject: a low old bedroom, a single candle on a wooden nightstand beside an old storybook with a worn leather cover, a window onto the dark grounds

storyboard.claim: Julia connects the bone to the family stories her grandmother told at bedtime.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candlelit bedroom with an old storybook on the nightstand, the bedtime story set.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the bone to memory, away from the yard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows where the stories were told: the bedroom, at bedtime.

image.subject: Caroline, a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, stands alone in a grey 1692 village street while townspeople turn their backs

storyboard.claim: Her ancestor Caroline was condemned as a witch in 1692.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline alone in a grey village street, townspeople turned away from her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts a face on the bedtime story the previous frame introduced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives Caroline her look and shows her isolation in 1692.

image.subject: an old stone church cemetery gate, locked with an iron chain, a rough wooden fence beyond the graves and a dark field outside it, no figure

storyboard.claim: The town would not bury a convicted witch in the church cemetery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A locked stone churchyard gate, with the cemetery closed to her and the dark field outside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Caroline's condemnation to where she was refused burial.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the locked gate that keeps her out of holy ground.

image.subject: Archie Eldridge, a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, carries a long bundle wrapped in dark cloth across a moonlit field toward a timber house in the dead of night

storyboard.claim: Archie secretly carries her remains back to the house at night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Archie in a dark coat walking a moonlit field carrying a cloth-wrapped bundle toward the house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the refusal of burial with the husband taking her home instead.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Archie as the one who buries her on the property, in secret.

image.subject: a low mound of fresh dark earth in an overgrown backyard, no marker or stone, a spade leaning against a tree in the grey dusk

storyboard.claim: She was buried in an unmarked grave in the backyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bare mound of fresh earth with no stone, a spade against a tree.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows where the bundle from the night walk ended up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the grave in the same yard Julia is walking, with no marker.

storyboard.claim: Inheriting the estate is more than wealth, land, and old buildings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A short list on screen naming wealth, acreage and historic architecture, the things people expect to inherit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Steps back from the grave to the general idea of inheritance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the claim that the inheritance includes something the list does not show.

image.subject: an old yellowed property deed with a red wax seal and dark ink signature, lying on a candlelit wooden desk beside a folded stack of household letters

storyboard.claim: You inherit the legal and moral debts of your ancestors, not only the property.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An aged deed with a wax seal on a candlelit desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the list back to a single legal object: the deed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The document is the legal side of an inheritance that also carries crimes.

image.subject: close-up of dark garden soil with a tarnished old silver coin and a small pale bone fragment half-buried in it

storyboard.claim: The land you own is made of secrets buried to protect the family's status.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dark soil with a tarnished coin and a bone fragment pressed into it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the deed into the ground it describes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The coin links the wealth and the burial in one object.

image.subject: a water-stained ceiling of an old wooden house with a metal bucket catching drips on a bare floorboard, no figure

storyboard.claim: Ordinary house inheritance worries are taxes and leaky roofs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A water-stained ceiling with a bucket catching drips on the floor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches to the everyday worries a buyer would have.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the normal burden with the one the house carries.

image.subject: a dim hallway of a timber house with one closed bedroom door at the far end and a single candle on a windowsill, no figure

storyboard.claim: People do not think they are inheriting the physical space where harm happened.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dim hallway with a closed bedroom door at the far end.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the roof to the rooms themselves.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the closed door as the trace of what the house holds.

image.subject: a padlocked wrought-iron gate across a dirt path in an overgrown yard, a rusted chain wrapped twice around the bars, no figure

storyboard.claim: The living relatives are ruthless about protecting that land.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A padlocked iron gate across a dirt path, chained shut.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the house to the land it protects, now guarded.
storyboard.addedInformation: The padlock shows the family locks the yard the way it locks the house.

image.subject: Ethel, an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, stands in a doorway of a timber house looking out

storyboard.claim: Julia's great-aunt Ethel is the one who knows the cost of the buried ground.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel in a doorway, grey bun and dark cardigan, stern face turned to the yard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the person who guards the land.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives Ethel her look for the rest of the book.

image.subject: Ethel, an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, stands at a kitchen window looking down at a dug patch of yard

storyboard.claim: Ethel learns that Julia has dug up a bone in the yard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel at a window, watching the dug patch of ground below.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Carries the discovery from Julia to the aunt who will confront her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ethel is shown watching the spot where the bone was found.

image.subject: Ethel, elderly, thin, grey bun, dark cardigan, stern face, corners Julia in a narrow timber-house hallway, one finger raised; Julia, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, backs against the wall

storyboard.claim: Ethel corners Julia with a menacing stare.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel leaning toward Julia in a narrow hallway, Julia pressed against the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the window to a face-to-face confrontation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the menace in their positions, not only in words.

storyboard.claim: Ethel warns Julia never to disturb Caroline's grave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The warning set as text on a dark card, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Ethel's threat its exact words after the confrontation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The warning ties the family threat to the ghost.

image.subject: a faint, translucent young woman in a plain linen cap and dark period dress drifts across a moonlit overgrown yard toward a fresh mound of earth, no clear face

storyboard.claim: Ethel uses the ghost story to protect the land from being dug up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A faint Caroline drifting across the moonlit yard toward the grave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns Ethel's threat into a picture of the ghost she invokes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the supernatural story as a tool the aunt is using.

storyboard.claim: A ghost story is being used as security for a crime scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The punchline set as text on screen, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the ghost image into a joke about protection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the ghost story as a crime-scene defence.

storyboard.claim: The host asks what this means for Julia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The question set as text on screen, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR JULIA?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from Ethel to Julia's choices.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next stretch as a question about Julia's response.

image.subject: Julia, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, crouches over a pale pelvic bone in black dirt, one hand moving toward her coat pocket, the dark timber house behind her

storyboard.claim: Any normal person would call the police right away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia crouched over the bone, her hand moving toward her coat pocket.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question by putting Julia back at the bone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her hand toward her pocket shows the obvious action she is considering.

storyboard.claim: She does not say it is her great-great grandmother from 1692.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The line set as text on a dark card, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the words Julia would not say about the bone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the family claim the reason she does not call.

image.subject: two raccoons at the edge of dark woods sniffing a shallow hole in the yard, a dim timber house far behind them

storyboard.claim: Julia would rather leave the bone for the raccoons than call the police.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two raccoons at the woods edge sniffing a shallow hole, the house dim behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the joke into a picture, the raccoons being left to deal with it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the absurd choice the narration names.

image.subject: a heavy chestnut front door in a dim hallway with a candle in a wall sconce, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry Ziegler has already told Julia the rules of the trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry in a tweed jacket, polite but intense, beside the chestnut door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings in the museum man whose offer depends on the land.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives Henry his look and places him at the house.

image.subject: yellow police tape stretched across the heavy chestnut front door of a timber house at dusk, no figure

storyboard.claim: If police find remains, the whole property becomes a state crime scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Yellow police tape across the chestnut front door at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows Henry's warning with what would happen if the police came.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the tape closing the house itself.

left.label: THE LAW
left.subject: a legal document with a red wax seal on a dark desk beside a closed leather book

right.label: THE MONEY
right.subject: a tall stack of gold coins on a dark wooden table, candlelit

storyboard.claim: Julia must weigh reporting the remains against the museum's millions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A legal seal on one side and a stack of coins on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the crime-scene consequence into the choice she faces.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two pulls, duty and money, as objects on each side.

image.subject: a low old bedroom with a narrow bed, a worn quilt, a window onto the dark grounds and an empty armchair by the fireplace, no figure

storyboard.claim: Her grandmother is 85, frail and confused, and her home is the emotional leverage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A narrow old bed and quilt in a low bedroom, empty chair by the fire.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the choice to the grandmother's home.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the grandmother's home the place at stake.

image.subject: a timber house at night lit by harsh white floodlights, a yellow backhoe parked on the churned front lawn, no figure

storyboard.claim: A forensic dig with floodlights and backhoes would kill her grandmother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Harsh floodlights on the house and a backhoe parked on the churned lawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what the excavation the narration describes would look like.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the cost of digging visible on the grandmother's house.

image.subject: a pale bone wrapped in cloth being set back into a hole, the dark earth half-filled around it, the timber house in the background, no figure

storyboard.claim: Julia chooses the estate's financial safety over the truth of the bones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cloth-wrapped bone lowered back into a hole, the soil half-filled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the choice into the act of putting the bones back.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the compromise as a reburial.

storyboard.claim: The house makes you an accomplice to its crimes just by living there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The line set as text on screen, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE HOUSE MAKES YOU AN ACCOMPLICE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk on the complicity the reburial made concrete.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the chunk's verdict on the house and the people who live in it.
